Bar graph with confidence intervals

ci.bars.Rd

Draws a bar graph of cell means with confidence intervals. Usually called through the bgraph option of anovakun.

Usage

ci.bars(dat, design, factnames = NA, conf.level = 0.95, inn.tier = "cind",
  out.tier = NA, main = NULL, ylab = NULL, barmin = 0)

Arguments

dat

A data frame as used inside anovakun (subject column, factor columns, and the dependent variable in long format).

design

A character string giving the design, e.g. "As", "sA", "AsB". Letters before s are between-subjects factors and letters after it are within-subjects factors.

factnames

Names of the factors. If NA, letters are used.

conf.level

Confidence level.

inn.tier

Type of the inner confidence interval (e.g. "cind").

out.tier

Type of the outer confidence interval, or NA.

main

Main title of the plot.

ylab

Label of the y axis.

barmin

Lower end of the bars.

Value

A bar graph is drawn on the current graphics device as a side effect.

Author

Ryuta Iseki (author); packaged by Koji Kosugi.

References

ANOVA-kun: https://riseki.cloudfree.jp/?ANOVA%E5%90%9B

See also

anovakun

Examples

dat <- data.frame(
  A    = c("a1", "a1", "a1", "a2", "a2", "a2"),
  b1c1 = c(12, 13, 11, 18, 17, 15),
  b1c2 = c( 9, 10, 10, 12, 14, 13),
  b2c1 = c(14, 14, 13, 16, 15, 18),
  b2c2 = c(13, 12, 15, 15, 14, 15)
)
# Usually drawn through the bgraph option of anovakun()
anovakun(dat, "AsBC", 2, 2, 2, bgraph = c("cind", "cin"))

# Direct use on the long-format data that anovakun() builds internally
long <- anovakun(dat, "AsBC", 2, 2, 2, tech = TRUE, data.frame = TRUE)$DATA.FRAME
ci.bars(long, "AsBC", inn.tier = "cind", out.tier = "cin", main = "AsBC design")
